_doc: SQL Server -> PostgreSQL conversion knowledge for every construct the T-SQL parser (codebase-documenter sql_parse.py / sqlscan) reports. level: auto = schema-conversion tools (AWS DMS Schema Conversion / SCT, sqlglot) or a one-to-one rename handle it, review only; rewrite = a PostgreSQL equivalent exists but the code must be rewritten by hand and retested; redesign = no PostgreSQL equivalent, the feature has to be replaced by a different design (extension, application code, another AWS service). hours = manual-equivalent [low, high] per occurrence, before the AI factor. Keys are exact construct labels; prefix_defaults cover 'fn: X', 'global: @@X' and 'data type: x' labels not listed. Sources: AWS SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL migration playbook, PostgreSQL documentation, Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL limitations.

levels.auto: converted by schema-conversion tooling or a direct rename; review only
levels.rewrite: PostgreSQL has an equivalent, but the code is rewritten by hand and retested
levels.redesign: no PostgreSQL equivalent: replace with a different design (extension, application code or another service)

cursor.pg: PL/pgSQL cursor or, better, a set-based query / FOR row IN SELECT loop

TRY/CATCH.pg: BEGIN ... EXCEPTION WHEN ... END block; ERROR_*() -> GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS

MERGE.pg: MERGE (PostgreSQL 15+, no OUTPUT/$action until 17) or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT

OUTPUT clause.pg: RETURNING (no OUTPUT INTO a table variable; use a CTE)

PIVOT.pg: conditional aggregation (FILTER / CASE) or tablefunc crosstab()

FOR XML.pg: xmlagg / xmlelement, or string_agg for the FOR XML PATH('') concatenation idiom

RAISERROR.pg: RAISE EXCEPTION / RAISE NOTICE (severity and state have no equivalent; error numbers become SQLSTATE codes)

THROW.pg: RAISE EXCEPTION ... USING ERRCODE (callers that test SQL Server error numbers must test SQLSTATE)

TOP.pg: LIMIT / FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY

TOP WITH TIES.pg: FETCH FIRST n ROWS WITH TIES (PostgreSQL 13+)

TOP PERCENT.pg: window function (percent_rank / ntile) or a computed LIMIT

WAITFOR.pg: pg_sleep(); WAITFOR RECEIVE (Service Broker) has no equivalent

GOTO.pg: no GOTO in PL/pgSQL: restructure with loops, EXIT/CONTINUE and exception blocks

savepoint.pg: SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT; inside functions use nested BEGIN ... EXCEPTION blocks

transactions.pg: transaction control only in procedures (CALL), not in functions; no nested-transaction counting

IDENTITY_INSERT.pg: INSERT ... OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE, then setval() the identity sequence

table variable.pg: temporary table, array of composite type or CTE

temp table.pg: CREATE TEMP TABLE (session-scoped; must be created before use, no #name scoping per procedure)

inserted/deleted.pg: NEW / OLD in row triggers, or transition tables (REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS ...) in statement triggers

TRY_CONVERT.pg: no TRY_ cast: a helper function with an exception block, or pg_input_is_valid() (PostgreSQL 16+)

TRY_CAST.pg: no TRY_ cast: a helper function with an exception block, or pg_input_is_valid() (PostgreSQL 16+)

PARSE.pg: to_date / to_timestamp / to_number with an explicit format (culture argument has no equivalent)

full-text.pg: tsvector / tsquery with GIN indexes (different ranking, language and CONTAINS/FREETEXT semantics), or OpenSearch

OPENQUERY/OPENROWSET.pg: postgres_fdw / other foreign data wrappers (not on every managed service), or move the integration to the application / AWS Glue

cross-database.pg: PostgreSQL cannot query another database in one statement: merge into schemas of one database, or use postgres_fdw / dblink

USE database.pg: no USE: one connection per database; switch schemas with search_path

row-level security.pg: CREATE POLICY row-level security (different predicate model)

temporal table.pg: no system-versioned tables: history table maintained by triggers, or the temporal_tables extension

temporal query.pg: FOR SYSTEM_TIME queries rewritten against the trigger-maintained history table

memory-optimized.pg: no In-Memory OLTP: ordinary tables (UNLOGGED for transient data); natively compiled procedures become PL/pgSQL

columnstore.pg: no columnstore indexes: BRIN indexes, partitioning, or an analytics store (Redshift / a columnar extension)

partitioning.pg: declarative partitioning (PARTITION BY RANGE / LIST / HASH); partition functions and schemes have no direct form

CLR.pg: SQL CLR assemblies cannot run in PostgreSQL: rewrite as PL/pgSQL, an extension, or move the logic into the .NET application

graph MATCH.pg: recursive CTEs, or Apache AGE / Amazon Neptune for graph workloads

Service Broker.pg: no Service Broker: LISTEN/NOTIFY, a queue table with SKIP LOCKED, or Amazon SQS

event notification.pg: event triggers / LISTEN-NOTIFY or application-level events

BULK INSERT.pg: COPY (server files) or \copy / Npgsql binary import (client files); aws_s3 extension on RDS/Aurora

XML index.pg: no XML indexes: expression indexes on xpath() results, or store the queried values in columns / jsonb

data type: xml.pg: xml type exists, but .value()/.query()/.nodes()/.modify() methods become xpath() / XMLTABLE

method call on column (xml/spatial/hiera.pg: xpath() / PostGIS ST_* functions / ltree operators instead of column methods

SET options.pg: ANSI_NULLS / QUOTED_IDENTIFIER / ARITHABORT have no equivalent; SET options become GUC settings where they exist

SET option OFF.pg: code relying on ANSI_NULLS OFF (= NULL comparisons) or CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL OFF behaves differently: rewrite the predicates

table type.pg: composite type + array parameter (no table-valued parameters); callers change too

synonym.pg: no synonyms: views, search_path or wrapper functions

index.pg: CREATE INDEX (INCLUDE and filtered WHERE supported; CLUSTERED has no equivalent)

INSERT EXEC.pg: INSERT ... SELECT * FROM set-returning function (procedures cannot feed INSERT)

AT TIME ZONE.pg: AT TIME ZONE exists, but Windows time-zone names must become IANA names

ODBC escape.pg: standard SQL function calls instead of {fn ...} escapes

CONVERT.pg: CAST / to_char / to_date; CONVERT style codes have no equivalent

database options.pg: ALTER DATABASE SET options differ: review each (READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT is PostgreSQL's default behaviour)

logins/users.pg: CREATE ROLE; Windows logins become IAM / Kerberos / password authentication

permissions.pg: GRANT / REVOKE (DENY has no equivalent: revoke and grant selectively)

computed column.pg: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED (no virtual / non-persisted columns before PostgreSQL 18; expression must be immutable)

COLLATE.pg: ICU or citext collations; SQL Server's case-insensitive default has no default equivalent, so equality, LIKE and unique keys can change behaviour

FILESTREAM.pg: no FILESTREAM: bytea / large objects, or move files to Amazon S3 and keep the key

table hints.pg: remove (PostgreSQL has no table hints; pg_hint_plan extension if a plan must be forced)

NOLOCK.pg: remove: MVCC readers never block; code that relied on dirty reads sees committed data only

UPDATE ... FROM.pg: UPDATE ... FROM exists but the target must not be repeated in FROM; alias rules differ

dynamic SQL.pg: EXECUTE format(...) USING ... in PL/pgSQL (quote_ident / %I for names); review every dynamic statement for T-SQL text

extended procedure (xp_).pg: no extended procedures (xp_cmdshell, xp_sendmail ...): move to the application, AWS Lambda or a job scheduler

system procedure (sp_).pg: catalog queries / built-in functions instead of sp_ procedures (sp_rename -> ALTER ... RENAME, sp_getapplock -> pg_advisory_lock)

string concatenation with +.pg: || or concat(); note NULL || x is NULL while concat() skips NULLs

LIKE character class.pg: LIKE has no [a-z] classes: SIMILAR TO or ~ regular expressions

distributed transaction.pg: no distributed transactions (MSDTC) on managed PostgreSQL: two-phase commit is not available on RDS/Aurora by default; use an outbox / saga pattern

OPENROWSET BULK.pg: COPY / aws_s3.table_import_from_s3 instead of reading server files

external table (PolyBase).pg: foreign data wrappers or AWS Glue / Athena instead of PolyBase external tables

GETDATE.pg: now() / clock_timestamp() (now() is fixed per transaction)

SYSDATETIMEOFFSET.pg: clock_timestamp() (timestamptz does not keep the offset)

NEWSEQUENTIALID.pg: uuidv7() (PostgreSQL 18) or an extension; ordering semantics differ

DATEDIFF.pg: date arithmetic / EXTRACT(EPOCH ...); DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, so results differ unless rewritten carefully

DATEDIFF_BIG.pg: date arithmetic / EXTRACT(EPOCH ...); DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, so results differ unless rewritten carefully

DATEPART.pg: EXTRACT / date_part (week and weekday numbering differ: DATEFIRST)

SWITCHOFFSET.pg: AT TIME ZONE (offsets are not stored with timestamptz)

TODATETIMEOFFSET.pg: AT TIME ZONE (offsets are not stored with timestamptz)

PATINDEX.pg: regexp_instr() (PostgreSQL 15+) or substring with a regular expression

STUFF.pg: overlay(); STUFF(... FOR XML PATH('')) concatenation becomes string_agg()

LEN.pg: length() (LEN ignores trailing spaces; length() does not)

FORMAT.pg: to_char() with PostgreSQL format patterns (.NET format strings and cultures have no equivalent)

STRING_AGG.pg: string_agg() (WITHIN GROUP becomes ORDER BY inside the call)

SUSER_SNAME.pg: current_user / session_user (Windows account names do not exist; audit columns change meaning)

HOST_NAME.pg: inet_client_addr() / application_name (client host name is not available)

ERROR_NUMBER.pg: SQLSTATE (five-character codes, not numbers): every caller that branches on numbers changes

ERROR_SEVERITY.pg: no severity levels: map to SQLSTATE classes

ERROR_STATE.pg: no state: drop or map to SQLSTATE

XACT_STATE.pg: no equivalent: an exception block always rolls back its subtransaction; restructure error handling

ISJSON.pg: IS JSON (PostgreSQL 16+) or a cast inside an exception block

CHECKSUM.pg: no equivalent hash (values differ): md5 / hashtext; anything that stored or compared CHECKSUM values must be recomputed

BINARY_CHECKSUM.pg: no equivalent hash (values differ): md5 / hashtext; anything that stored or compared CHECKSUM values must be recomputed

HASHBYTES.pg: pgcrypto digest() / sha256() (same algorithms; byte encoding of nvarchar input differs: UTF-16 vs UTF-8)

COMPRESS.pg: no GZIP function: compress in the application (stored compressed bytes stay readable only there)

DECOMPRESS.pg: no GZIP function: compress in the application (stored compressed bytes stay readable only there)

LOG.pg: ln(x) / log(base, x): argument order differs from LOG(x, base)

ISNUMERIC.pg: regular-expression test or pg_input_is_valid() (PostgreSQL 16+); ISNUMERIC accepts '$', ',' and 'e'

ISDATE.pg: pg_input_is_valid(x, 'date') (PostgreSQL 16+) or a helper with an exception block

TRY_PARSE.pg: helper function with an exception block

GREATEST.pg: GREATEST() (ignores NULLs, SQL Server 2022 GREATEST also ignores NULLs)

GROUPING_ID.pg: GROUPING(a, b, ...) returns the same bitmask

FILESTREAM.pg: no FILESTREAM: Amazon S3 + key column

PATHNAME.pg: no FILESTREAM: Amazon S3 + key column

GET_FILESTREAM_TRANSACTION_CONTEXT.pg: no FILESTREAM: Amazon S3 + key column

@@IDENTITY.pg: INSERT ... RETURNING (@@IDENTITY also sees trigger inserts; RETURNING does not)

@@ERROR.pg: exception blocks (errors abort the statement; there is no error-code polling)

@@TRANCOUNT.pg: no transaction nesting count: restructure transaction ownership (procedures with COMMIT, or the application)

@@DATEFIRST.pg: no DATEFIRST: compute weekdays with EXTRACT(ISODOW)

@@NESTLEVEL.pg: no nesting level: pass depth explicitly

money.pg: numeric(19,4) (PostgreSQL money is locale-dependent; avoid it)

datetime.pg: timestamp(3) (datetime rounds to 1/300 s; equality on stored values can differ)

datetimeoffset.pg: timestamptz stores the instant, not the original offset: add an offset column if the offset matters

uniqueidentifier.pg: uuid (sort order differs from SQL Server's)

timestamp.pg: rowversion has no equivalent: xmin system column (EF Core Npgsql UseXminAsConcurrencyToken) or a trigger-maintained version column

rowversion.pg: rowversion has no equivalent: xmin system column (EF Core Npgsql UseXminAsConcurrencyToken) or a trigger-maintained version column

sql_variant.pg: no variant type: jsonb, text plus a type column, or separate typed columns

bit.pg: boolean (queries and code comparing to 0/1 change) or smallint

hierarchyid.pg: ltree extension or a parent-id / path column; GetAncestor / IsDescendantOf rewritten

geography.pg: PostGIS geography (extension); STDistance etc. become ST_* functions

fn:.pg: check the PostgreSQL equivalent of this built-in function

global:.pg: check the PostgreSQL equivalent of this @@ variable
